tagline: Leading independent power producer in Argentina with diversified generation portfolio
hero_kpi_rationale: Installed capacity of 6,938 MW positioning CEPU as Argentina's largest private electricity producer, foundation of its competitive position and future growth.

kpis.name: Installed Capacity
kpis.explanation: Total power the company can generate in megawatts.
kpis.description: Total capacity distributed across thermal, hydroelectric and renewable sources. Positions CEPU as Argentina's largest private producer.
kpis.signal: Market leader in Argentina with 6,938 MW.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated from electricity sales and related services.
kpis.description: Revenues of $783 million in 2025, driven by energy generation sold primarily in hard currencies.
kpis.signal: Revenues almost entirely in US dollars, reducing currency risk.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Key performance indicator used by management and analysts to assess operational profitability, reflecting cash generation capacity.
kpis.signal: Solid adjusted EBITDA despite volatile Argentine economic environment.

kpis.name: Net Leverage
kpis.explanation: Net debt divided by adjusted EBITDA, measures repayment capacity.
kpis.description: Net leverage ratio of 0.3x in 2025, indicating low debt relative to operational cash flow generation.
kpis.signal: Very low leverage, reflecting solid financial position and financing flexibility.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on new projects, assets and technology modernization.
kpis.description: Investments of $202 million in 2025, notably for solar projects and battery energy storage systems (BESS).
kpis.signal: Strategic Capex in 2025 to strengthen renewable capacity and modernization.

kpis.name: Generation Volume
kpis.explanation: Total quantity of electricity produced in gigawatt-hours.
kpis.description: Total volume generated in 2025, distributed across thermal (74%), hydro (17%) and renewable (9%).
kpis.signal: Annual production of 18,598 GWh, supported by strong diversified installed capacity.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €3,669.79 billion in latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €493.03 billion in latest year

kpis.name: Renewables Share
kpis.explanation: Percentage of installed capacity sourced from renewable energy.
kpis.description: 8% of installed capacity in 2025 sourced from renewable sources, including solar projects such as Cafayate and San Carlos.
kpis.signal: Progressive growth in renewables with acceleration of new solar projects.

kpis.name: Battery Energy Storage Development
kpis.explanation: Battery storage capacity under development or in operation.
kpis.description: 205 MW BESS project launched in 2025, scheduled to enter service late 2026, strengthening flexibility of Argentine electrical grid.
kpis.signal: Launch of 205 MW battery storage, sign of technological innovation and grid flexibility.

risks.title: Dependence on natural gas supply
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned centrally in the document, with strong language ("critical", "significant"). Gas dependence is structural and worsening with supply scarcity in Argentina. This category weighs heavily on thermal generation operations.

risks.title: Tariff regulation and delayed payments by CAMMESA
risks.score_rationale: Risk documented in detail, with alarming language on payment delays ("LVFVD", "no fixed payment date"). Trend is deteriorating. Argentine electricity market regulation concentrates major operational cash flow risk.

risks.title: Increased competition in energy market
risks.score_rationale: Risk clearly identified in outlook, with affirmative language on new market entrants. Trend is increasing competition, notably with renewable energies. Directly impacts market share and pricing.

risks.title: Dependence on Argentine government decisions
risks.score_rationale: Risk repeated multiple times, with strong language ("government intervention", "public emergency"). Law 27,742 strengthens executive power. This structural risk dominates the company's operating framework.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of critical energy systems
risks.score_rationale: Risk introduced in new chapter (Item 16.K), with serious language on growing threats. Trend is rising cyber-risks. Directly concerns operational integrity of power plants.

risks.title: Risks related to expansion and construction projects
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in outlook and linked to delays or budget overruns. Language is cautious but recurring. Trend is stable, but critical for future growth.

risks.title: Shortage of skilled labor
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned briefly but in context of talent competition. Language is moderate. Trend is stable, but strategic for complex technical operations.

risks.title: Exposure to environmental and regulatory risks
risks.score_rationale: Risk cited in forward-looking factors, with increasingly strong language on environmental regulations. Trend is rising. Affects operating costs and future permits.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in documents provided.
evidence: No AI reference in presentations or 10-K/20-F reports
Absence of AI automation or predictive analytics projects
Focus on physical energy generation and electrical infrastructure, not digital
